name: AI Cloud Agents
description: Event-driven automation rules — subscribe to platform events (email arrivals, schedule ticks, custom signals) and run multi-step actions across other extensions when conditions match.

tools.name: skeleton_refresh_rules
tools.description: User's automation rule stats + platform event catalog (read by LLM each turn).

tools.name: list_automations
tools.description: List automation rules with full detail: who owns each one (user_id), when it was created, its trigger event and cron schedule, run counters, success rate and current failure. Filter by owner (admins), status, event type, free text, creation date range, or narrow to scheduled/failing/never-triggered rules.

params_schema.description:
Filter for listing automation rules.

Every filter is optional and they COMBINE (logical AND). Admins may
additionally scope by owner; for non-admins the owner filters are
ignored (they only ever see their own rules).

status.description: Optional filter: 'active', 'paused', or 'error'. Omit for all.
status.title: Status

mine.description: Show ONLY the calling user's own rules. Set this whenever the user says 'my automations' / 'мои автоматизации' / 'the ones I created'. The owner id is taken from the authenticated session, so it is always correct — NEVER try to guess the caller's imperal_id and pass it via user_id instead. Admins included: an admin asking for THEIR rules wants this, not the whole tenant.
mine.title: Mine

user_id.description: ADMIN ONLY — show rules belonging to SOMEBODY ELSE. Accepts a full imperal_id (imp_u_...) or a fragment of it. Use when asked 'which automations belong to <user>'. For the caller's OWN rules use mine=true instead.
user_id.title: User Id

event_type.description: Filter by trigger event, e.g. 'system.scheduled', 'email.received'. Substring match, so 'email' matches every email.* trigger.
event_type.title: Event Type

search.description: Free-text search across prompt, interpretation, action text and last_error (case-insensitive).
search.title: Search

scheduled_only.description: Only cron/scheduled rules (those carrying a cron schedule).
scheduled_only.title: Scheduled Only

failing_only.description: Only rules that currently carry a last_error or have failures.
failing_only.title: Failing Only

never_triggered.description: Only rules that have NEVER fired (trigger_count=0). Useful for spotting dead or orphaned automations.
never_triggered.title: Never Triggered

created_after.description: Only rules created at/after this ISO date, e.g. '2026-08-01'.
created_after.title: Created After

created_before.description: Only rules created at/before this ISO date, e.g. '2026-08-31'.
created_before.title: Created Before

limit.description: Max rules to return (1-500). Applied AFTER filtering and sorting.
limit.title: Limit

params_schema.title: ListAutomationsParams

AutomationRule.description:
One automation rule, as projected by ``handlers._rule_summary``.

ADDITIVE SDL migration: every existing field is kept verbatim (same
name AND same type) so the panels / sidebar / list-item builders that
read ``rule_id`` / ``prompt`` / ``status`` / ``trigger_count`` etc.
keep working unchanged. The canonical SDL ``id`` / ``title`` / ``kind``
are populated from the existing fields via a ``mode="before"``
validator, so existing
``ActionResult.success(data={"rules": [_rule_summary(r), ...]})`` calls
construct this model without any caller-side changes.

Field → role map:
  id              <- rule_id   (core.id)
  title           <- prompt    (core.title)
  status          <- status    (core.status; active/paused/error)
The trigger/throttle counters, timestamps and owner are kept as their
EXISTING string/int shapes and carry custom ``automations.*`` roles —
they are NOT remapped onto facets whose field types differ (e.g. the
standard ``time.created_at`` is a ``datetime`` and ``people.owner`` is a
``Ref``, which would reject the existing ISO-string / id-string values).
``sdl.WorkflowState.state`` mirrors the lifecycle state for state-machine
aware platform consumers; ``sdl.Prioritized`` is mixed in (all-optional)
for forward-compat with rule urgency. No existing field is renamed.
AutomationRule.title: AutomationRule

return_schema.description:
``list_automations`` return shape — a REAL ``sdl.EntityList[AutomationRule]``
(``items=[...]``, ``x-sdl="entity-list"``). The legacy ``{rules:[dict], ...}``
wrapper is GONE; the handler now returns
``data={"items":[...], "total": n, "admin_view": bool, "filter": {...}}``.

``admin_view`` and ``filter`` are kept as additive typed fields on the
EntityList so the existing scalars survive verbatim for the narrator.
return_schema.title: AutomationListResponse

tools.name: create_automation
tools.description: Create a new automation rule from rules.available_events skeleton.

StructuredAction.description:
WS2 grounded action — the resolved (app_id, tool, args) the rule runs.
Optional on create: when present the GW persists it instead of free text.

For `conn-ssh` (the user's own servers) this is more than an optimisation:
the stored action IS the pre-authorization. A write-tier server tool
(run_command / write_file / edit_file) runs unattended ONLY through a stored
action, because then the command is the literal one the user approved and
can re-read in the panel. Described in words instead, it cannot run.

app_id.description: Extension that owns the tool, from the user's live scope (or 'conn-ssh' for the user's servers)
app_id.title: App Id

tool.description: @chat.function name the user can actually invoke
tool.title: Tool

args.description: Well-formed args for the tool (conn-ssh: connection_id + e.g. command)
args.title: Args

StructuredAction.title: StructuredAction

event_type.description: Trigger event from rules.available_events skeleton (e.g. email.received, notes.created, system.scheduled)
event_type.title: Event Type

action_description.description: What to do when triggered, in natural language
action_description.title: Action Description

action.description: Resolved (app_id, tool, args) for grounded persistence (WS2). Omit to keep NL action.

return_schema.title: AutomationActionReceipt

user_id.description: Optional — report on a single owner (id or fragment) instead of all.

tools.name: bulk_automation_action
tools.description: Pause, resume or DELETE several automation rules in one call. Target them by explicit rule_ids, or select them with the same filters as list_automations (owner, status, event, text, never-triggered, failing). Always run with dry_run=true first to see exactly what would be affected. Admins may act on other users' rules.

params_schema.description:
Apply one lifecycle operation to SEVERAL rules in a single call.

Either pass explicit ``rule_ids``, or select rules with the same
filters ``list_automations`` accepts. Selection filters are the safe
way to act on 'every failing rule of user X' without enumerating ids
by hand. Admins may target other users' rules; non-admins are always
confined to their own.

rule_ids.description: Explicit rule IDs to act on. Omit to select by filter instead.
rule_ids.title: Rule Ids

user_id.description: ADMIN ONLY — restrict the selection to this owner (id or fragment).
user_id.title: User Id

status.description: Restrict selection to rules in this status ('active'/'paused'/'error').
status.title: Status

event_type.description: Restrict selection to this trigger event (substring match).
event_type.title: Event Type

search.description: Restrict selection to rules whose text matches this term.
search.title: Search

never_triggered.description: Restrict selection to rules that have never fired.
never_triggered.title: Never Triggered

failing_only.description: Restrict selection to rules that currently carry a failure.
failing_only.title: Failing Only

dry_run.description: Preview only — report exactly which rules WOULD be affected and change nothing. Defaults to TRUE: a bulk lifecycle operation never fires by accident. Set false (with confirm=true) to apply.
dry_run.title: Dry Run

confirm.description: Required for 'delete'. Without it a delete is refused and only reports what WOULD be deleted (safe dry run).
confirm.title: Confirm

params_schema.title: BulkRuleParams

return_schema.description:
Receipt for ``bulk_automation_action`` — what was selected, what
actually happened, and what failed, per rule id.

Field names mirror the handler's return dict verbatim
(I-EXT-RECORD-FIELD-NAMING-SYMMETRIC).
return_schema.title: BulkActionReceipt
